s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging breast swelling with signs of inflammation and skin involvement
salient_findings: Tender swelling in the outer half of the right breast
Overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction
Skin fistula with pus extruding and orange peel appearance of the skin
key_facts: 42-year-old woman
3-month history of gradually enlarging right breast swelling
No history of tuberculosis or tuberculous contact
No family history of cancer
Five children
Using a contraceptive device for 5 years
Tender swelling in the outer half of the right breast
Overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction
Mobile ipsilateral axillary lymph node measured 2.5 cm
No nipple discharge
Infectious workup was strictly normal
Ultrasonography and mammography showed an ACR-4 lesion
Empirical fluoroquinolone was started
Skin fistula developed with pus extruding after 7 days
Breast MRI revealed multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a rapidly enlarging breast mass, overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction, along with the development of a skin fistula and the imaging findings of multiple lesions with irregular thick walls, is most consistent with inflammatory breast cancer, which is a highly aggressive and rare form of breast cancer.

rejected.label: Granulomatous mastitis
rejected.why: While granulomatous mastitis can present with similar symptoms, the lack of response to empirical antibiotics and the development of a skin fistula, along with the imaging findings, make inflammatory breast cancer a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Breast abscess
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more complex and suggestive of a malignant process rather than a simple breast abscess.

rejected.label: Idiopathic granulomatous mastitis
rejected.why: Similar to granulomatous mastitis, the patient's presentation and imaging findings are more suggestive of a malignant process.

rejected.label: Necrotizing granulomatous mastitis
rejected.why: While necrotizing granulomatous mastitis can present with similar symptoms, the patient's imaging findings and lack of response to empirical antibiotics make inflammatory breast cancer a more likely diagnosis.
